We need a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction to synthesize target SMILES: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. This looks like a methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe a Diels-Alder adduct). The hint says Diels-Alder reaction is forward. So retrosynthesis: break the bicyclic ring into diene and dienophile. The template likely corresponds to a Diels-Alder retro. We need to find a template that matches target and gives two precursors: a diene and a dienophile (maybe a methyl acrylate). Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken maybe "C-C double bonds" and formed maybe "C-C double bonds"? Actually Diels-Alder breaks two C=C bonds (in diene) and forms two new C-C sigma bonds, and also breaks a C=C in dienophile. So forward reaction forms sigma bonds, breaks double bonds. In retrosynthesis, we break sigma bonds to form double bonds. So functional_groups_broken (forward) = "C-C double bonds"? Wait forward: Diels-Alder forms C-C sigma bonds, breaks C=C double bonds. So forward broken: C-C double bonds. So in retrosynthesis we want to break sigma bonds, which is opposite. The tool expects forward broken groups. So we set functional_groups_broken = ["C-C double bonds"] maybe. Also functional_groups_formed = []? The dienophile may have carbonyl etc. Let's just search with broken C-C double bonds. Already did that and got many templates. The first result seems to be a Diels-Alder template (reaction_id 1914385). It shows product_smiles matches our target? product_smiles: [CH3][O][C](=O)[C@]12[CH2][CH]=[CH][CH2][C@H]1[C@]2? Let's compare. The product SMILES in result: '[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C@:5]12[CH2:6][CH:7]=[CH:8][CH2:9][C@H:10]1[C:11](=[O:12])[CH2:13]2' That is methyl ester of a bicyclic unsaturated ketone, matches our target (C=O at position). Our target: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. Yes same. So template_id is the template_hash? Actually they give template_hash and reaction_id. We need template_id to use in route. Probably template_id is the reaction_id? The tool expects template_id string. Might be the template_hash? Usually template_id is numeric. We'll use reaction_id 1914385 as template_id.

Now we need to apply this template to get precursors. Use apply_template with molecule SMILES and template_id "1914385".
